A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with 32 complete pages including Appendices A–E. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support comparison of all text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original transformer experiments on algorithmic tasks in Section 4 and Appendix C, plus evaluations of DeepSeek-R1 and o1-mini in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including accuracy measurements, sensitivity analyses, and pretrained-LLM reasoning-trace measurements.

M1.justification: The transformer models and CoT procedures in Sections 2–4 and Appendices B–C are unchanged, including the multiplication and graph-search constructions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same parity, addition, multiplication, median, and DAG-reachability tasks. Appendix D retains the same pretrained-LLM task coverage.

E2.justification: The full, shortened, dot-by-dot, and no-CoT comparisons retain the same participants. Figure 11 also retains the same NTT-versus-naive multiplication comparison.

E3.justification: Input lengths, dataset splits, sample sizes, model configurations, training budgets, decoding procedures, and evaluation metrics are unchanged throughout the experimental sections and appendices.

E4.justification: The CoT-shortening experiments, sensitivity analyses, multiplication digit analysis, held-out evaluations, and qualitative LLM-trace inspection are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Reporting practices are identical, including three-run averages for parity and graph reachability and three random seeds for median. No uncertainty estimates or statistical procedures are added or removed.

E6.justification: All result entries, plotted curves, and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports 99.83% accuracy for both 8-digit and 16-digit multiplication and 99.96% for 14-digit multiplication in both PDFs.

T1.justification: Definition 4.1 corrects the malformed input notation {−0+1}^N to {0,1}^N. This is a typographical repair: v1 already describes PARITY as a bit-string problem in Sections 1–2. The mathematical assumptions, bounds, reasoning, and proofs are substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unconditional UHAT CoT lower bounds, their tightness up to logarithmic factors, and practically trainable matching constructions.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including the worst-case and UHAT restrictions, the relationship to softmax experiments, and the open question about shorter learnable CoTs in other transformer models.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, data-generation procedures, and LLM prompts. Document link targets are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The references and research positioning in Section 5.2 and Appendix E are identical, including the comparisons with subset-parity and globality-degree research.

P1.justification: v2 repairs the notation typo in Definition 4.1 and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. There are no other text changes or structural revisions.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12 and Table 1 retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. The document layout and appendix organization are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The Definition 4.1 correction improves local clarity, but v1 already unambiguously identifies the intended bit-string parity task. With all proofs, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information unchanged, this isolated typo repair and version-stamp update do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
